title: T1090.001 — Proxy - Internal Proxy
subtitle: Watch an internal proxy attack unfold in eight steps.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Beachhead
steps.caption: The attacker exploits an internet-facing service and lands on an internal server, R1. R1 sits in a server zone that many hosts can reach and that is allowed to send traffic out. The SOC sees only a normal-looking web session.
steps.defender: without an endpoint agent on R1, the foothold is invisible at this point.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: One quiet exit
steps.caption: The attacker installs a beacon on R1. It opens one outbound link through the company firewall to the C2 server on the internet. The SOC sees one new egress flow from a server. It looks like ordinary HTTPS.
steps.defender: one flow, no content visibility without TLS inspection.

steps.title: Inside channel
steps.caption: On R1, the beacon starts an SMB named-pipe listener. Infected hosts inside the network will use this pipe to reach R1. Pipe creation is a local event; the firewall sees nothing.
steps.defender: without Sysmon event 17/18 or an EDR pipe event, this step never appears in the SIEM.

steps.title: Victim A joins
steps.caption: A phishing mail infected workstation A earlier. Its beacon cannot reach the internet. It finds the pipe on R1 and sends its C2 traffic through it. The SOC sees plain east-west SMB from A to R1, which happens all day.
steps.defender: the C2 content hides inside a trusted protocol.

steps.title: Victim B joins
steps.caption: A second workstation joins the same pipe. Now two victims are controlled through R1, but the firewall still shows only the one egress flow from step 2.
steps.defender: the egress count stays flat while the number of victims grows. That gap is the story of this technique.

steps.title: The gap, drawn out
steps.caption: The attacker now commands three hosts and needs only one external connection. If the attacker loses that one link, R1 keeps the inside channel alive and can re-connect later.
steps.defender: blocking one IP does not close the attack. The mesh lives inside.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Detection
steps.caption: The EDR reports a new named pipe on R1 from a service host. Zeek shows many hosts opening SMB sessions to one server, plus odd pipe names. The correlation rule joins pipe event, fan-in, and the single egress flow. A high-severity alert fires with the whole chain pre-built.
steps.defender: this is Sigma rule 2 plus rule 6 in section 5.5.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Respond and fix
steps.caption: The SOC isolates R1 and kills the pipe listener. The firewall team blocks the C2 address. The team hunts for the pipe name on every host to find victims A and B, then rebuilds R1 from a clean image.
steps.defender: contain the relay, then sweep the mesh - in that order.
